text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node/gpu-12 ephemeral usage at 98% (scratch), multiple pod eviction events detected. Affected pods: modelcache-serve-5, runtime-gpu-2, log-collector-7. Possible cascading restarts. Paging on-call.

anna: ack — I'm on it. Seeing increased OOM/killed messages in kubelet logs.

julia: I can help with modelcache. Which model shards got evicted?

anna: initial glance: modelcache-serve-5 restarted 4x in last 6m. kernel OOM kills target processes (CUDA) after pod eviction. Also log-collector grew to 120GB under /scratch/logs.

kevin: tagging customers: serving latency spikes ~3x, 503s for some heavy-traffic tenants. Notified PG about degraded routing.

anna: grabbing `kubectl describe pod modelcache-serve-5 -n redwood` now, posting relevant bits:

anna: ```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From     Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----     -------
  Warning Evicted    5m    kubelet  The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Container runtime attempted to free disk by evicting pods.
  Normal  Killing    5m    kubelet  Killing container with id docker://modelcache because it exceeded address space
```

julia: modelcache writes checkpoints to /scratch/checkpoints by default; looks like rotated files and a recent stuck checkpoint write (3GB every 30s) due to background sync.

anna: inspecting node usage via `ssh gpu-12` then `du -sh /scratch/* | sort -h` shows:

anna: ```
70G /scratch/logs
45G /scratch/checkpoints
12G /scratch/tmp
```

mike: first mitigation: cordon node to stop scheduling new pods, drain non-critical pods (log-collector), and free up space. Plan to restart/evict modelcache gracefully onto other nodes.

kevin: agree. Also need to minimize customer impact: switch traffic for heavy tenants to fallback-model (smaller quantized) on the router. Can someone trigger the route fallback?

julia: I'll push a quick rollout to fallback-model for the two affected routes. ETA ~2m.

anna: executing node cordon and targeted drain for log-collector

anna: ```sh
kubectl cordon gpu-12
kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='app=log-collector' -n redwood
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started drain job for node gpu-12 (job id 8832).

anna: after drain, I cleaned up old logs: removed rotated logs older than 7d and truncated active log file `log-collector/current.log` to free space. Deleted one stale debug dump (`/scratch/logs/core.dump.2026-03-15`) ~4.3G.

julia: paused modelcache background checkpointing (`kubectl exec -c sidecar modelcache-serve-5 -- scale-checkpointing --pause`) — that reduced writes.

kevin: traffic reroute to fallback-model in place. Telemetry shows error rate dropping, p95 latency returning toward baseline.

mike: we still have CUDA errors in pod logs for runtime-gpu-2: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE` followed by container restart. That looks like restart storm related to eviction timings.

anna: restarting runtime-gpu-2 once after freeing disk to let it reinitialize GPU state. If it flaps again, we'll mark node unschedulable and move remaining pods.

anna: ```sh
kubectl delete pod runtime-gpu-2 -n redwood
```

kevin: customer impact update: support reported 2 customers saw degraded QPS with elevated 503s for ~8m window. No data loss reported. Incident impact: partial degradations for < 1% tail traffic.

mike: handing off to next on-call (mike) in 10m for sustained monitoring and post-incident next steps. I'll assemble initial incident ticket and severity assessment.

anna: creating incident doc in the ops runbook and linking logs. Key notes: ephemeral full due to combined long-retention logs + runaway checkpointing; kubelet eviction removed modelcache pods leading to CUDA state corruption after restart (container restarts + kernel OOM).

julia: suggested immediate remediation checklist posted: mount /scratch with reserved capacity, enable logrotate compression + retention 7d, move heavy checkpoints to a different PV (non-ephemeral), and add liveness probe that checks modelcache KV health to avoid noisy restarts.

mike: assigning follow-ups:
- anna: upload sanitized kubelet logs + core dump sample to incident ticket
- julia: PR to change default checkpoint path and add pause-on-sigterm behavior for modelcache
- kevin: customer comms draft for affected tenants, include timeline and mitigation steps

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0315-17, severity: S2. Assigned owners: anna, julia, kevin.

anna: handing monitoring to mike. I'll remain available for any follow-up. :thumbsup:

mike: taking ownership for the next hour. Will monitor metrics and confirm node remains cordoned until fix is applied.

kevin: thanks everyone. Postmortem candidate: yes. Root cause hypothesis: logrotate misconfig + checkpoint process that ignores SIGTERM leading to large contiguous writes on ephemeral. Long-term: enforce per-node ephemeral quota, change default storage paths for model artifacts, and add alert for >85% ephemeral usage that starts preemptive cleanup script.

julia: one more note — backup plan if node flaps again: scale down model replicas and warm-start on healthy nodes using cached weights to avoid heavy checkpoint writes.

mike: OK closing thread for now, will re-open if we see new evictions. :white_check_mark:
